q: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic ____ (or membrane).
e: Surface tension is the tendency of the surface of a liquid to behave like a stretched elastic skin (or membrane). Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the ____ substance.
e: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of the same substance. same is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: For example, cohesion makes water molecules pull together making the water surface to stretch like an elastic ____.
e: For example, cohesion makes water molecules pull together making the water surface to stretch like an elastic skin. skin is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Surface tension is the reason a water ____ and it is able to stride along water surface without sinking.
e: Surface tension is the reason a water strider and it is able to stride along water surface without sinking. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are also able to rest on water without sinking although their density is ____ than that of water.
e: Paperclips, razor blades and light coins are also able to rest on water without sinking although their density is higher than that of water. The still fluid sits at higher pressure than the fast stream.

q: Surface tension is defined as the force per unit ____ that acts across any line on a surface tending to pull the surface apart.
e: Surface tension is defined as the force per unit length that acts across any line on a surface tending to pull the surface apart. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: The SI unit of surface tension is newton per ____ ($N m^{-1}$).
e: The SI unit of surface tension is newton per metre (N m⁻¹). Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Surface tension can also be referred to as a force because it is the tension between liquid ____.
e: Surface tension can also be referred to as a force because it is the tension between liquid molecules. Surface tension γ is the force per unit length along a line in the surface, γ = F/l.

q: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or ____ material.
e: Capillary action is defined as the spontaneous flow of a liquid into a narrow tube or porous material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the ____ forces between the liquid and tube material.
e: Capillary action is caused by the combination of cohesive forces of the liquid and the adhesive forces between the liquid and tube material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of same substance; whereas, adhesion refers to forces between molecules of ____ substances.
e: Cohesion refers to forces between molecules of same substance; whereas, adhesion refers to forces between molecules of different substances. different is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently ____ in diameter.
e: In order for wicking to occur, a tube needs to be sufficiently small in diameter. small is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Capillary action is also the rise or depression of a liquid in a narrow tube of small cross-sectional area, like the spaces between the fibres of a towel or the openings in a ____ material.
e: Capillary action is also the rise or depression of a liquid in a narrow tube of small cross-sectional area, like the spaces between the fibres of a towel or the openings in a porous material. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: The rise of water underneath the ground is also the example of ____ action.
e: The rise of water underneath the ground is also the example of capillary action. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Capillary action helps bringing water up into the ____.
e: Capillary action helps bringing water up into the roots. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: When a glass tube with a small inside diameter is dipped into water, the water rises into the tube; for example, a glass tube with a bore of about 1 mm in diameter, the water will rise to a height ____ cm.
e: The blank is 5. That word is the one that completes the idea about glass tube small inside diameter dipped.

q: The smaller the bore, the ____ the water will rise.
e: The smaller the bore, the higher the water will rise. The still fluid sits at higher pressure than the fast stream.

q: Liquids that rise in small bore tubes inserted into the liquid are said to ____ the tube, whereas liquids that are depressed within thin tubes below the surface of the surrounding liquid do not wet the tube.
e: The blank is wetting. That word is the one that completes the idea about Liquids rise small bore tubes inserted.

q: Water is a liquid that wets glass capillary tubes; ____ is one that does not.
e: Water is a liquid that wets glass capillary tubes; mercury is one that does not. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: Capillarity does not occur for non-____ liquids.
e: Capillarity does not occur for non-wetting liquids. Capillary rise is h = 2γ cosθ / (ρgr); a narrower tube or larger γ gives a larger height.

q: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the ____ between glass and water causes a thin film of water to be drawn up over the inner and outer surfaces of the tube.
e: When a glass tube is dipped into water, the adhesion between glass and water causes a thin film of water to be drawn up over the inner and outer surfaces of the tube. adhesion is the word that belongs in that blank.

q: Since the adhesive force is greater than cohesive force, water level rises until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for ____ forces to overcome these intermolecular forces.
e: Since the adhesive force is greater than cohesive force, water level rises until there is a sufficient mass of liquid for gravitational forces to overcome these intermolecular forces. gravitational is the word that belongs in that blank.
